form.title: Narthex Decisions
form.overviewBlurb: The open questions of SPEC.md v0.3.0 (§11), and five items to confirm the assumptions of §13. Recommendations come first.

sections.title: Decide
sections.blurb: Questions only you can answer. Open ones first.

sections.title: Read
sections.blurb: The documents behind these questions, all in the repo.

sections.title: Act
sections.blurb: Only what needs you: review and merge, run, send, or discuss with someone.

sections.title: Claude's queue
sections.blurb: What I'm doing or will do next, in order. No action needed; comment to reorder or stop one.

items.title: What is Narthex's final name?
items.lead: Narthex is a codename (R1). A final name needs a trademark and domain search, and should suit the book.
bullets: No candidate has been checked against trademarks, domains, npm or GitHub.
The book's title may want the same name.
items.rec: search first; a name that fails a trademark check costs a rename later.
options: Run a trademark and domain search first (recommended)
Keep Narthex as the final name

items.title: Where do newcomers' repositories live?
items.lead: Sign-up guides a newcomer to create a GitHub account (R13). A hosted git option would skip that step.
bullets: A guided GitHub account keeps every repo user-owned, as R7 says.
Hosted git also suits regulated customers wanting a managed, audited store.
Hosting means taking custody of customers' code.
items.rec: a guided GitHub account in v1; hosted git later, when a customer needs it.
options: Guided GitHub account now, hosted git later (recommended)

items.title: What are Narthex's pricing and business model?
items.lead: Hosting, sign-up plans and limits per organisation all wait on this.
bullets: Bloque's teams come first (R12), so the pilot shows what teams actually use.
Narthex runs no model of its own in v1, so model costs stay with the user.
items.rec: decide after the Bloque pilot, with usage figures in hand.

items.title: Which sector profiles ship first?
items.lead: Every profile keeps ids, invariants, amendments, decisions and the trace chain.
bullets: product: SaaS and APIs; acceptance criteria as scenarios.
oss-ledger: Bloque's case; product plus ledger invariants with property tests.
protocol: fault model, safety and liveness properties, formal or executable reference.
items.rec: product and oss-ledger; they cover Bloque's teams, the first customers.

items.title: May an executable or formal spec outrank SPEC.md?
items.lead: Ethereum's consensus specs are executable Python; protocols often make a formal model the reference.
bullets: Per profile: protocol yes, others no.
SPEC.md still states which artefact is normative.
items.rec: yes, where the profile says so; the prose spec links to the normative artefact.
options: Yes, where the profile says so (recommended)

items.title: Does an agent count as an independent reviewer?
items.lead: Regulated profiles require review by someone other than the author. A lead plus agents needs a rule.
bullets: A fresh reviewer agent is independent of the authoring agent, not of the lead's intent.
Assessors expect a person for safety levels.
items.rec: agents count for product and oss-ledger; a person is required under regulated profiles.
options: Agents for product and oss-ledger; a person for regulated (recommended)

items.title: Does every amendment bump the spec version?
items.lead: Kippu kept v0.2.0 through four amendments, because a minor bump on v0 implied too much.
bullets: Proposed: below v1.0.0, a patch bump, listed in the amendment.
From v1.0.0, a bump on every amendment.
items.rec: patch bumps below v1.0.0; the version still moves, without overstating the change.
options: Patch bump below v1.0.0, a bump from v1 (recommended)

items.title: What does an agent do when it finds a spec gap?
items.lead: Kippu stopped and applied nothing unruled. aledgent and usage subscriptions built the conservative reading meanwhile.
bullets: Proposed: build meanwhile only if it is the plan's reading or stricter.
Never change SPEC or PLAN before the ruling.
Otherwise stop the task and raise the item.
items.rec: the reconciliation above; it keeps work moving without applying anything looser than the plan.
options: Build only the plan's or a stricter reading (recommended)

items.title: How are tests named?
items.lead: Kippu and aledgent put AC and INV ids in test names. On usage subscriptions you rejected that three times.
bullets: Proposed: a per-project house rule.
Default: plain names, ids in a comment, read by the trace checks.
items.rec: a per-project setting, defaulting to plain names with ids in comments.
options: Per project; default plain names, ids in comments (recommended)

items.title: When does a builder's change need an engineer?
items.lead: Alarms fire on a failed tagged check, a change to another team's identifier, or an unknown touchpoint.
bullets: Green: merges on the builder's approval.
Amber: the identifier's owner reviews.
Red: blocks and pages an engineer, with check, product spec and diff.
items.rec: three tiers; engineers see only what touches what they own.
options: Every change reviewed by an engineer

items.title: Which builder and which product pilot Narthex at Bloque?
items.lead: Bloque's teams are the first customers (R12). A real non-engineer building a real operation proves the chain.
bullets: Smallest useful: one operations flow on Bloque's core.
Needs the core's capabilities described first, by what each is for.
options: An operations flow on the core (details in notes)

items.title: Who checks the legal side of sector material, and when?
items.lead: Narthex ships open standards' text, and supplementary material for the rest (R4). Derived material may still raise copyright questions.
bullets: ISO, IEC, RTCA and SAE texts are copyrighted.
Checklists and clause mappings are Narthex's own work, but cite closed texts.
items.rec: a lawyer, before the first pack with material derived from a standard ships.
options: A lawyer, before the first standards-derived pack (recommended)
A lawyer, before any pack ships

items.title: Confirm the 9 trust and access assumptions?
items.lead: Trust and access: who may do what, and what an agent may do alone. Nobody has ruled these yet.
bullets: One organisation with several teams shares one spec in v1 (ASM-1).
Agents sign in with OAuth 2.1 and get a short-lived token per task (ASM-4).
Commits come from the human or the signed app; snapshots use expiring links (ASM-5, ASM-6).
Agents may act on defaults of reversible items; they merge only when told (ASM-34, ASM-43).
Guard hooks refuse rule breaks; no certification is claimed (ASM-45, ASM-29, ASM-22).

items.title: Confirm the 18 chain and method assumptions?
items.lead: Chain and method: how the steps run and how work is checked. Nobody has ruled these yet.
bullets: Each step has a fixed brief and an exit a script decides (ASM-24).
A review comes before merge; no turn waits on CI; each agent has its own worktree (ASM-8, 9, 15).
The threat model uses STRIDE; AI checks use the user's model access (ASM-3, ASM-7).
Questions come in passes; changes that touch no identifier skip spec and plan (ASM-12, ASM-47).
Validation is the product-spec owner's answer on the form (ASM-56).

items.title: Confirm the 15 form behaviour assumptions?
items.lead: Form behaviour: how items, answers and the inbox work. Nobody has ruled these yet.
bullets: One form per project; the repo records every answer (ASM-11, ASM-30, ASM-31).
Items are JSON; rulings live in the log and amendments (ASM-32, ASM-33).
Items may be deferred, carry a due scope, and be seeded from a project (ASM-19, ASM-20, ASM-21).
Claude push notifications come first; "Discuss first" builds an agenda page (ASM-35, ASM-36).
A ref opens in a modal; anchors come from identifiers; evidence is tagged (ASM-37, ASM-38, ASM-39).

items.title: Confirm the 9 docs and profiles assumptions?
items.lead: Docs and profiles: living documents, sector profiles and sector material. Nobody has ruled these yet.
bullets: specsite renders the living docs: Starlight sites and HTML editions first (ASM-25).
Editions are flagged stale when their source moves on (ASM-14).
A profile is a data file with pinned editions and the universal parts kept (ASM-27).
The trace graph and amendment diff are in v1; file names and prefixes are fixed (ASM-44, ASM-52, ASM-53).
A legal check applies only to material from copyrighted standards (ASM-55).

items.title: Confirm the 5 packaging and experiments assumptions?
items.lead: Packaging and experiments: how Narthex ships and how experiments are kept. Nobody has ruled these yet.
bullets: The skills ship as one Claude Code plugin, plus an Agent Skills install path (ASM-40).
The repository stays local until a second project runs it (ASM-41).
House-rule defaults ship with Narthex, extended by a project file (ASM-46).
Experiment logs are committed under experiments/ (ASM-48).
An agent may drop an experiment and report it (ASM-49).

items.title: Is the spec-profile work next?
items.lead: You called it the first assessment: an open-source fintech ledger and a safety-critical BFT system need different specs.
bullets: Profiles as data: required sections, notation, trace rules, exports, gates.
specsite and the spec skill enforce the chosen profile.
options: Yes, next, ahead of the other amendments (recommended)

items.title: Which profiles ship first?
items.lead: Every profile keeps ids, invariants, amendments, decisions and the trace chain.
bullets: oss-ledger: Bloque's case; product plus ledger invariants with property tests.
protocol: fault model, safety and liveness properties, formal or executable reference.
safety: one profile with a level (DAL, ASIL, SIL, IEC 62304 class).

items.title: May an executable or formal spec outrank SPEC.md?
items.lead: Ethereum's consensus specs are executable Python; protocols often make a formal model the reference.
bullets: Per profile: protocol yes, others no.
SPEC.md still states which artefact is normative.
options: Yes, where the profile says so (recommended)

items.title: Does an agent count as an independent reviewer?
items.lead: Regulated profiles require review by someone other than the author. A team of one lead plus agents needs a rule.
bullets: A fresh reviewer agent is independent of the authoring agent, not of the lead's intent.
Assessors expect a person for safety levels.
options: Agents for oss-ledger and product; a person for regulated (recommended)

items.title: Sections follow a decision: Read, Decide, Act
items.lead: Pablo on aledgent's form, relayed on 2026-10-13: context first, then the ruling, then the action.
options: Read → Decide → Act, then Updates and Later

items.title: Who is v1 for?
items.lead: The answer sets the licence, the name, and how much polish the first release needs.
bullets: Own projects: fastest; aledgent's method, generalised.
Open source: needs docs, examples and a neutral house-rules default.
Product: needs hosting beyond claude.ai and several answerers.
items.rec: your own projects first; open it once a second project runs on it.
options: My own projects first, open later (recommended)

items.title: Is the decision inbox also a product on its own?
items.lead: The form needs nothing from the other modules: any lead with open questions could use it.
bullets: As a module, it ships inside the plugin and can be used alone (REQ-WF-17).
As its own product, it needs its own name, page and hosting.

items.title: Under which licence is the code released?
items.lead: Only matters once anything leaves your machine (OQ-20).
bullets: MIT or Apache-2.0: easiest to adopt; Apache adds a patent grant.
AGPL: keeps hosted forks open.
None yet: stay private until v1 works.
options: None yet; decide at first release (recommended)
items.applied: Swimming on Code licence rule (STATE.md); amendment 0004

items.title: Keep the working name "SDD Studio" for now?
items.lead: The name appears in the plugin id, the repo and every skill's namespace.
items.applied: SPEC v0.3.0 (R1); final name is OQ-1

items.title: Where does the form live in v1?
items.lead: aledgent's form is a claude.ai artifact with a database, answered from your phone and read back by the agent directly.
bullets: Artifact: works today; tied to claude.ai and Claude Code's artifact tools.
Self-hosted page: any browser, but needs a backend and auth.
GitHub issues: familiar, but no defaults, sub-tabs or outbox.
items.rec: artifact now, behind a storage interface so another host can follow.
options: Self-hosted page with a small backend

items.title: Is the repo the record of every answer?
items.lead: The store is where answers arrive; the archive in `decisions/responses/` is what the log and amendments cite.
bullets: Repo as record: answers survive the host, and git shows when each arrived.
Store as record: one fewer step, but history depends on the host.
options: The repo; the store is only an inbox (recommended)

items.title: Which format do agents write items in?
items.lead: Agents write items far more often than people do.
bullets: JSON: no dependencies, strict, easy to validate.
YAML: easier to read, needs a parser.
Markdown files: readable per item, harder to check.

items.title: Do rulings also get their own decision-record files?
items.lead: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) keep one short Markdown file per decision: context, choice, consequences. Here the log lists every answer and amendments carry the reasoning.
bullets: Log only: one place to read, no duplication.
One file per ruling: ADR-compatible, more files to keep in step.
options: Also one ADR-style file per ruling

items.title: May agents apply a default before you answer?
items.lead: On aledgent, low-stakes items carried a default and were listed below a divider so you could overrule them.
bullets: Only on reversible items.
Never on reserved items: outward actions, security, product rulings.
Every default is visible as 'Default applied'.
options: No, every item waits for you

items.title: Which channel carries notifications?
items.lead: One notice per publish, naming sections and counts.

items.title: Can people other than you answer items?
items.lead: On aledgent, DevOps and partner questions went through you.
bullets: v1: one answerer; items may name who should answer.
Later: per-item answerers, with each answer attributed.

items.title: Do "Discuss first" answers build a meeting agenda?
items.lead: Such answers stay open and are listed under 'To discuss' on the overview. An agenda page would group them for a call.
options: Yes, an agenda page from them (recommended)

items.title: How does an item open the spec at its anchor?
items.lead: The form already has a first version: a modal that shows just that section, with a link to the full page.
options: Iframe of the full page at the anchor

items.title: Are anchors taken from identifiers only?
items.lead: `REQ-DI-4` becomes `#req-di-4` wherever it is defined. Heading text changes; identifiers never do.
options: Yes, identifiers; headings get slugs too (recommended)

items.title: Must research and explainers tag their evidence?
items.lead: The two explainer pages tagged each claim Code, Measured, Plan, Inference or Not in code, with commit-pinned citations.

items.title: Specs are generated from the .md; shared tools are public repos
items.lead: Pablo's principles while building specsite, relayed by the aledgent session on 2026-10-13.
bullets: The `.md` is the source of truth; sites and editions are generated, never copied.
A tool other projects need is a public repo; reuse one that exists.

items.title: Is specsite SDD Studio's living-docs module?
items.lead: swimmingoncode/specsite renders SPEC, PLAN and amendments in Starlight with id anchors and links, plus single-file HTML editions.
bullets: Answers oq-13, oq-14 and oq-17, removed from this form.
Next on its roadmap: backlinks from decisions, a reference check, tombstones.
Its HTML editions published next to the form, so items open the spec in place.

items.title: Add a needs.json-compatible export to specsite?
items.lead: Lets traceability tools (sphinx-needs, DOORS) read our requirements without rewriting our Markdown.

items.title: How is the workflow packaged?
items.lead: Recommendation and reasons are in `notes/2026-10-03-packaging.md`.
bullets: Plugin: skills, hooks, agents and templates installed as one versioned unit.
Model to copy: diagram-design ships one repo as a Claude Code plugin and an `npx skills add` skill.
Custom harness: full control, but loses the artifact tools the form relies on.
items.rec: a plugin now; a harness only if the dispatch board needs one.
options: A custom harness on the Agent SDK

items.title: Where does the code live, and is there a remote?
items.lead: The repo is local only, and a remote is an outward action, so it waits for you. SDD Studio belongs to Swimming on Code, where specsite now lives.
bullets: Local: install from the folder through a local marketplace.
Swimming on Code org: public like specsite, MIT.
diagram-design shows the public-repo path: marketplace plus `npx skills add`.
options: Local until a second project runs it (recommended)
Public repo in the Swimming on Code org

items.title: Which project pilots it after SDD Studio itself?
items.lead: A pilot proves the skills carry no aledgent-specific content.
bullets: aledgent: real load, but mid-flight; retrofit the form and docs only.
A new Bloque project: clean start, every skill used.

items.title: How do dispatched agents run?
items.lead: One agent per feature, each in its own worktree, with the house rules in its brief.
bullets: Subagents in worktrees: what aledgent used; tied to one session.
Background sessions: survive the session, harder to track.
Cloud sessions: run unattended, need a remote.

items.title: When may an agent merge its own PR?
options: Only when its task says so, CI green (recommended)
items.lead: aledgent's rule: merge only when the task allows it, and only with CI green.

items.title: Which candidate additions join v1?
items.lead: The README lists eight. Two depend only on the three modules.
bullets: Traceability graph: requirement, decision, task, PR, test.
Amendment diff: spec versions with the decisions behind each change.
The rest (dispatch board, measurement ledger, risk register, meeting notes) need more.

items.title: Do hooks enforce the mechanical house rules from v1?
items.lead: A brief is text an agent can misread. A hook refuses the command.
bullets: Identity or signing overrides in `git commit`.
Pushes to protected or upstream repos.
Durable files under `/tmp`.
options: Yes, ship guard hooks in v1 (recommended)

items.title: Where do the default house rules live?
items.lead: Every brief carries the house rules in full (REQ-WF-11).
options: Plugin defaults, extended by a project file (recommended)

items.title: Is there a fast path that skips spec and plan for small changes?
items.lead: The main criticism of Spec Kit, Kiro and BMAD is ceremony: a small fix becomes stories and criteria.
bullets: Fast path: intake, then dispatch with a one-paragraph brief.
Anything touching a requirement or invariant still goes through amend.
options: Yes, for changes that touch no requirement (recommended)
No, every change follows the full flow

items.title: Bound experiments so only their outcome reaches the form
items.lead: Ruled on aledgent on 2026-10-04 and relayed here. Its inbox reached about 86 items, many superseded by the next experiment.
bullets: Each experiment keeps its own decision log and draft spec changes.
It ends with an outcome: adopt, adapt or drop, with numbers.
Only an adopted outcome is promoted: one amendment, one DEC, 1 to 3 questions.
Applied defaults sit collapsed; tabs count open items only.
items.origin: aledgent session, relaying Pablo's ruling of 2026-10-04

items.title: Are experiment logs committed to the repo?
items.lead: aledgent keeps them in a gitignored `.scratch/`. A dropped experiment's record must survive (REQ-CO-18).
bullets: Committed under `experiments/`: kept, reviewable, small files.
Gitignored scratch: no noise in git, but lost with the checkout.

items.title: May an agent drop an experiment without asking you?
items.lead: Adopt and adapt always come to you as one item. Drop changes nothing in the spec.
options: No, every outcome comes to me

items.title: Adopt amendment 0002's fourteen additions as written?
items.lead: Lessons from Kippu, aledgent and usage subscriptions that no project disputes. Nothing is applied until you rule.
bullets: Review step with read-only reviewers; told of every later change.
No agent ends a turn waiting on CI; dispatch resumes it.
Reserved numbers; one form per project with a publish lock.
A `provide` kind and fewer, larger passes per milestone.
Deferral with a reason, release scoping, import of existing projects.

items.title: What does an agent do when it finds a spec gap?
items.lead: Kippu stopped and applied nothing unruled. aledgent and usage subscriptions built the conservative reading meanwhile.
bullets: Proposed: build meanwhile only if it is the plan's reading or stricter.
Never change SPEC or PLAN before the ruling.
Otherwise stop the task and raise the item.
options: Build only the plan's or a stricter reading (recommended)

items.title: How are tests named?
items.lead: Kippu and aledgent put `AC-*`/`INV-*` ids in test names. On usage subscriptions you rejected that three times.
bullets: Proposed: a per-project house rule.
Default: plain names, ids in a comment, checked by the trace tool.
options: Per project; default plain names, ids in comments (recommended)

items.title: Does every amendment bump the spec version?
items.lead: The spec says yes. Kippu kept v0.2.0 through four amendments, because a minor bump on v0 implied too much.
options: Patch bump below v1.0.0, as written from v1 (recommended)

items.title: Who drafts and who applies a ruling?
items.lead: On Kippu one coordinator did both and became the bottleneck. Usage subscriptions asks the same (wf-apply).
bullets: Proposed: the agent that found the gap drafts the amendment item.
The session owning the spec applies it after your ruling.
Reviewers are told what changed.

items.title: Is "anyone builds on the core, spec as norm" v1?
items.lead: Non-engineers build products on the core through agents; the core's spec runs as checks; engineers review only on an alarm.
bullets: Adds two parties: builders and engineer reviewers.
Adds two modules: discovery and design, and guardrails.
Answers oq-1: v1 is for Bloque's whole team.

items.title: Which builder and which product pilot it?
items.lead: A real non-engineer building a real operation on the new core proves both modules.
bullets: Smallest useful: one operations flow on the rebuilt core.
Needs the core's functional archaeology written down first.
options: An operations flow on the core (details in notes)

items.title: Is our product mapping the discovery flow?
items.lead: The steps match neither Story Mapping nor Impact Mapping; they compose older ideas in a reuse-first order.
bullets: Function analysis of what exists, then a needs-met map.
Needs × components value matrix, then a business-model-style descriptor.
A reuse review, then a plain-language how-it-works page (from SPARC).

items.title: When does a builder's change need an engineer?
items.lead: Alarms fire on a failed check tagged with a core REQ or INV, a change touching one, or an unknown touchpoint.
bullets: Green: merges on the builder's approval.
Amber: the identifier's owner reviews.
Red: blocks and pages an engineer, with check, descriptor and diff.
options: Every change reviewed by an engineer

items.title: Ask the contact how the reference tool works
items.lead: Nothing about it is public. Its per-step agents may save us designing module (d) from scratch.

items.title: Which Swimming on Code type and accent does specsite use?
items.lead: The guidelines mark both as proposals and the design-system artifact is empty. v0.1 uses Pairing A and deep violet.
bullets: Pairing A: Barlow Condensed, Barlow, JetBrains Mono.
Accent: #6A3FD9.

items.title: The name screen came back medium risk: what next?
items.lead: US registers look clear in classes 9 and 42, but the exact .com, .dev, .ai and .io are taken and others use the name.
bullets: Users include a church SaaS, a BI vendor and a Claude Code MCP project.
npm, PyPI and crates.io names are free; GitHub handle taken; getnarthex.com looks free.
Not legal advice: a lawyer's clearance search is still needed.
options: Keep Narthex as codename; choose the final name later (recommended)
Pursue Narthex as final: lawyer clearance next

items.title: Open-source business models for Narthex
items.lead: Models, examples and risks, ranked for Narthex; input for OQ-3, which you'll decide after the Bloque pilot.

chain.label: OQ-3 in SPEC.md
chain.why: The open question and your ruling: decide the model after the Bloque pilot.
